DAY 116-118 — DE-ESCALATION, THEN RE-ESCALATION: US STRIKES IRAN. Through Jun 24-25 the strait was normalising fast: Kpler put confirmed Hormuz oil flows at ~4.8M bpd (the most since the Feb 28 attack, still below the ~15M pre-war pace), ~70 ships transited on Wednesday (+105% day-on-day), 20+ long-stranded tankers carrying ~35M barrels exited the Gulf, the Joint Maritime Information Center downgraded the Hormuz threat to 'moderate,' and the US Treasury waived sanctions on Iranian oil sales through August — pulling Brent down to ~$72, a four-month low near the ~$70 pre-war level (down >10% on the week). THEN THE CEASEFIRE CRACKED: on Jun 25 an Iranian/IRGC one-way attack drone struck the Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely as it exited Hormuz along the US/Oman-backed southern corridor near Oman — Trump said Iran fired four drones (three shot down), one hit the upper deck, no injuries, the ship sailed on — and the IMO paused its plan to evacuate ~11,000 stranded seafarers while Iran reiterated that ships must use only its northern route. Early Jun 26, at Trump's direction, US Central Command struck Iran: six aircraft hit four targets (Iranian missile and drone storage sites plus coastal radar along Iran's coast, around Sirik), calling Iran's drone attack 'unwarranted aggression' that violated the ceasefire and undermined freedom of navigation. US officials framed the strikes as calibrated — large enough to message on freedom of navigation, limited enough to avoid restarting the wider war — ending the ~2-week pause in US offensive ops that had held since Trump cancelled a third strike round on Jun 11. Trump warned of more; Iran vowed a 'harsh' response. OIL bounced from its ~$72 low toward ~$74 on the strikes but stayed far below the March wartime peak (Dubai crude record ~$166). INDIA: equity markets are shut Jun 26 for Muharram; the last session (Thu Jun 25) closed marginally up — Sensex 77,100.47 (+0.14%), Nifty ~24,056 — with FIIs +Rs 384 Cr and DIIs +Rs 5,748 Cr, and reopens Monday Jun 29 to price the escalation. West Asia War Day 118.

DAY 115 PM — RISK-OFF RETURNS EVEN AS THE 60-DAY ROADMAP FIRMS UP. The morning's 'contested de-escalation' calm soured through the session: Indian equities sold off despite cheaper oil — the Sensex closed down 893.39 points (-1.16%) at 76,200.68 and the Nifty fell ~1.16% to ~23,824 — after President Trump threatened to resume strikes on Iran and Tehran briefly walked away from the Burgenstock talks before returning, with an IT-sector overhang (Accenture's flagged Middle East hit) dragging Infosys, TCS, HCLTech, Wipro and Tech Mahindra, and Reliance adding pressure. STRUCTURALLY, THOUGH, THE TALKS HELD: the first Switzerland round concluded with mediators Qatar and Pakistan announcing a joint 60-day roadmap toward a final deal; both sides confirmed the agenda covered nuclear, Lebanon and the Strait; technical teams continue through the week under four formal working groups (Sanctions Termination, Nuclear Affairs, Iran Reconstruction & Economic Development, Monitoring & Implementation) and a high-level oversight committee. SANCTIONS STEP: the US Treasury issued a 60-day license authorising the production, sale and delivery of Iranian oil, including imports of Iranian crude to the US payable in dollars. OIL eased further to ~$77 Brent (WTI ~$74) as tankers increasingly transited Hormuz with tracking on and the market priced a faster return of Gulf barrels; Saudi and Qatari crude is heading back to terminals. HORMUZ stays Iran-declared-closed on paper, but the Jun 21 safe-passage communications mechanism is functioning and CENTCOM maintains 'Iran does not control the Strait.' STILL FRAGILE: Iran's MOU ratification is still awaited (vote expected this week), Netanyahu refuses to withdraw from southern Lebanon before a final deal, and war-risk insurance remains ~8x pre-crisis with several P&I clubs withdrawing cover. The separate, non-war Qatar Ras Laffan/Barzan blast (13 dead, all Indian and Pakistani nationals; LNG exports unaffected) remains the day's India human cost. West Asia War Day 115.

DAY 115 — CONTESTED DE-ESCALATION: OIL FALLS, TALKS RESUME, QATAR BLAST KILLS INDIANS. By the morning of Jun 23 the panic of the Jun 20 re-closure has cooled in markets even though the strait remains Iran-declared-closed. (1) US Central Command reported that 55 merchant ships transited the Strait of Hormuz on Jun 20 carrying ~16-17 million barrels of oil — which VP Vance called 'a record going back to even before the conflict started' — and CENTCOM's Capt. Tim Hawkins said 'Iran does not control the Strait of Hormuz; traffic continues to flow.' Reuters reported oil and LNG tankers sailing through on Monday as traffic slowly picked up. (2) The Switzerland talks that looked cancelled on Friday went ahead on Sunday (Vance arrived) — described as tense but constructive — producing a 60-day roadmap toward a final deal and a US-Iran 'communication line' to ensure safe passage for commercial vessels. Trump posted that there would be 'NO TOLLS' in the strait for the 60-day ceasefire 'unless they are imposed by and for the United States,' should a final deal not be completed. (3) Brent crude FELL ~3.6-4.3% over 24 hours to ~$78.1 as the market re-read the closure as symbolic leverage tied to the Lebanon ceasefire rather than a physical shutdown. INDIA: equities closed Jun 22 UP — Sensex 77,094 (+0.38%), Nifty 24,103 (+0.37%) — on easing crude and Middle East optimism (pharma, IT, Reliance leading); India confirmed three of its tankers carrying 860,000+ MT crossed Hormuz safely. SEPARATE, NON-WAR INDIA HUMAN COST: a technical explosion during a restart at Qatar's Ras Laffan / Barzan gas facility late Sun Jun 21 killed 13 and injured 66 — Qatar's energy minister confirmed all 13 dead were Indian and Pakistani nationals and ruled out any hostile cause; Qatar says LNG exports and Ras Laffan port are unaffected (Barzan supplies domestic gas). STILL FRAGILE: Iran's parliament is due to vote on ratifying the MOU ~Jun 23-25 (rejection would signal an indefinite reopening delay); Netanyahu refuses to withdraw from S. Lebanon before a final deal — the exact trigger Iran cited; war-risk insurance remains ~8x pre-crisis with several P&I clubs withdrawing cover. straits.live crisis-pressure composite holds at 92 (extreme); 30-day escalation forecast up to 61 (high). West Asia War Day 115.

DAY 112-114 — THE DEAL UNRAVELS: IRAN RE-CLOSES HORMUZ. Saturday June 20: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters (top joint military command) declared the Strait of Hormuz 'closed to vessel traffic' — less than 48 hours after the Islamabad MOU (signed in person at Versailles Jun 17 evening; finalised digitally in the first minutes of Jun 18). Tehran called it the 'first step of response to the enemy's breach of trust,' citing the United States' 'clear breach' of Article 1 of the MOU — specifically continued Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon and the failure of Israeli forces to withdraw — and warned that 'further measures will be planned' if aggression continues. THE CLOSURE IS DISPUTED: US Central Command says vessels are still transiting and it sees no evidence of a physical closure; VP JD Vance told Fox News 'the straits really are open.' Iran's OWN foreign ministry, hours before the military statement, told Tasnim shipping was 'operating normally' — an open contradiction between Tehran's diplomatic and military wings. ON THE WATER: millions of barrels of crude still moved through Hormuz over the weekend (Bloomberg, Jun 21); ~12 vessels crossed Friday and ~25 Thursday (the most since April) before the declaration; ~515 vessels remain anchored or stopped across the region. UKMTO (Jun 21) reported a tanker approached by a skiff carrying five armed individuals ~50nm southeast in the Gulf of Oman. DIPLOMACY STALLED: the planned Friday Burgenstock signing/talks were cancelled (Swiss foreign ministry, Jun 19) and Vance did not travel; the quadrilateral track (Iran, US, Pakistan, Qatar) that briefly resumed in Switzerland suspended after a single round, with Iran demanding a verified Lebanon ceasefire as a condition and saying the talks would exclude its nuclear programme. Trump renewed threats of US strikes 'unless Iran curbs its proxies in Lebanon,' threatened Hormuz tolls in the absence of a deal, and warned Tehran against closing the strait. MARKETS: Brent bounced back to ~$81.5 (from $78.31 on Jun 19, ~+1.4%); WTI opened the week ~+1.5% above $78. India (Goodreturns, Jun 22): Nifty ~24,108 (+0.39%), Sensex ~77,112 (+0.40%) — broadly steady, treating the closure as contested/posturing while oil physically keeps flowing, though the four-day relief rally (peaked Thu Jun 18, Nifty 24,168 / Sensex 77,410) has stalled. straits.live crisis-pressure composite: 92 (extreme); 30-day escalation forecast: 59 (elevated). The 'war is over / 60-day peace clock' framing from Jun 19 is now in serious doubt — Hormuz, the war's central lever, is contested again. West Asia War Day 114.

DAY 109-111 — MAJOR CORRECTION: THE MOU WAS SIGNED 2 DAYS EARLY, AT VERSAILLES, NOT BURGENSTOCK. Wednesday June 17 evening: President Trump PERSONALLY SIGNED the US-Iran memorandum of understanding during a state dinner at the Palace of Versailles, France (G7 sidelines), with French President Macron standing beside him. IRAN'S PRESIDENT MASOUD PEZESHKIAN also signed in person — distinct from the earlier digital signing Sunday Jun 15 by VP Vance and Parliament Speaker Qalibaf. PAKISTAN PM SHEHBAZ SHARIF confirmed: 'Islamabad MoU shall enter into force with immediate effect and, as a first step, the Islamic Republic of Iran will instantly reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and the United States of America will immediately lift the naval blockade.' military.d: Fox News, Investing.com, CBS News (June 17-19): In a surprise development, President Trump personally signed the US-Iran memorandum of understanding during a G7 state dinner at the Palace of Versailles on Wednesday evening, with French President Macron present — two days before the planned Friday Burgenstock ceremony. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian also signed in person, a step up from Sunday's digital signing by deputies (VP Vance and Parliament Speaker Qalibaf). Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif, lead mediator throughout, confirmed: 'Islamabad MoU shall enter into force with immediate effect and, as a first step, the Islamic Republic of Iran will instantly reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and the United States of America will immediately lift the naval blockade.' Al Jazeera later clarified that today's Burgenstock event 'is not just a ceremonial signing ceremony because the documents have already been signed. It is the official kickoff of the 59 days remaining for these sides to come to a conclusion.' The venue — owned by Qatar's Katara Hospitality, the same sovereign fund that helped mediate — previously hosted the 2024 Ukraine peace summit.

military.t: 14-POINT MOU REVEALED IN FULL: War Ends All Fronts incl. Lebanon. Iran Reaffirms No Nuclear Weapons; Uranium Down-Blended Under IAEA. Hormuz 'Will NOT Return to Pre-War Conditions' — Fee-for-Service Model Persists. $300B Fund DENIED by Trump.
military.d: Al Jazeera, Newsweek, Bloomberg (June 17-18): The full 14-point MOU was revealed Wednesday via a US official's call with reporters (Iran has not independently confirmed every detail). Key provisions: immediate/permanent end to war on all fronts including Lebanon; mutual sovereignty respect and non-interference; Iran 'reaffirms that it shall not procure or develop nuclear weapons,' with enriched uranium stockpile to be 'down-blended on site under the supervision of the IAEA' via a mechanism still 'to be mutually agreed.' On Hormuz, Iran's lead negotiator Ghalibaf stated plainly: 'the Strait of Hormuz will not return to pre-war conditions' and Iran will 'receive a fee for services' to shipping — confirming the PGSA-style toll framework will persist in some form even after the formal blockade lifts. Trump separately denied earlier reports of a $300 billion US-funded reconstruction package for Iran, saying the US is 'not investing 10 cents' — the deal instead permits third-party/outside investment into Iran contingent on compliance. Many implementation specifics — the exact nuclear down-blending mechanism, Hormuz fee structure, sanctions-lifting sequencing, and reconstruction terms — are now subject to the 60-day Burgenstock talks beginning today.

military.t: KHAMENEI AUTHORISED THE DEAL RELUCTANTLY — 'A Different View' But Accepted After Assurances. US Lawmakers Both Parties Flag Verification + Missile Programme Concerns. Brent $78.31 Friday (-1.6%). WTI $74.75.
military.d: NewsNation, Investing.com (June 18-19): Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said Thursday he had authorised the MOU signed by Presidents Pezeshkian and Trump, despite personally holding 'a different view,' after receiving assurances from Pezeshkian and senior officials that Iran's rights and the interests of the 'Resistance Front' would be safeguarded. Pezeshkian, as SNSC head, accepted personal responsibility for protecting Iran's interests and pledged not to yield to 'excessive demands' in future talks — a signal of likely internal friction during the 60-day negotiation period. Separately, US lawmakers from both parties raised concerns about the deal: the nuclear verification mechanism remains undefined, and Iran's ballistic missile programme is not addressed in the 14 points at all. Trump confirmed he will send the deal to Congress for review. Markets continued pricing the deal as broadly durable but with residual uncertainty: Brent fell 1.6% to $78.31 Friday, WTI fell 1.7% to $74.75 — both above the pre-war ~$70 baseline. IAEA Director-General Grossi welcomed the interim deal: 'Now the technical work starts.'

The four-day rally through Wednesday's close (Nifty 24,085.70, +3.99% cumulative; Sensex 77,155.62, +4.50% cumulative; VIX 13.18) reflects the deal's substance, not the specific Versailles-vs-Burgenstock signing venue/timing detail. Pakistan PM's 'immediate effect' confirmation on the blockade lift and Hormuz reopening is, if anything, a stronger durability signal than markets had Wednesday morning — heads-of-state signatures carry more weight than the earlier deputy-level digital signing. The fuel price cut timeline (petrol Rs4-6/L, LPG Rs80-100/cylinder, expected within 3-4 weeks pending mine removal) is unaffected. India's 18,000+ stranded Gulf seafarers and 562 crew on Indian-flagged vessels should see accelerated repatriation given the formal 'immediate effect' blockade lift. Doesn't even matter what the deal says." AXIOS SEQUENCING BRIDGE: Hormuz Phase 1 (no tolls + mines + blockade lifted) → nuclear Phase 2 (negotiations during 60 days). India June 1: GIFT Nifty direction critical. Trump signature = Brent $80-85, Nifty +1,500-2,000 pts, Rupee 91-92. West Asia War Day 92.

DAY 91 FRI 9:15AM IST — LAST DAY OF MAY 2026. BRENT $92.56 (6:35AM ET) — DOWN 19% IN MAY. WORST MONTHLY BRENT LOSS SINCE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. Off 20% from 2026 peaks. TRUMP'S FOUR MOU CONDITIONS (CNBC confirmed): (1) Iran never have nuclear weapon. (2) Immediately open Hormuz UNRESTRICTED + WITHOUT TOLLS. (3) REMOVE remaining mines. (4) Allow US to UNEARTH AND DESTROY enriched uranium buried under rubble. Trump HAS NOT SIGNED MOU. UBS (Thursday note): "little evidence of short-term improvement in vessel traffic or energy flows." Crude loadings inside Gulf "EXTREMELY LOW." US GAS PRICES: fell 14 CENTS since $4.56/gallon peak — biggest one-day drop since November 2008 Great Recession. IRAN: will only discuss nuclear clauses ONCE Phase 1 MOU cemented. BESSENT: declined to confirm deal details. Thursday: Iran ballistic missiles toward Kuwait intercepted. IRGC warning shots at 4 vessels. India: Brent $92 = Rs 2.3L Cr annual import bill saving vs April $126 peak. OMC near-breakeven on petrol. Month-end Friday. West Asia War Day 91.

DAY 90 THU 8:15AM IST. 60-DAY MOU REACHED BY NEGOTIATORS — extend ceasefire + start nuclear negotiations. TRUMP STILL HAS TO APPROVE. Axios confirmed. CNBC confirmed. IRAN STATE TV: Tehran agreed draft MOU — Hormuz to pre-war levels — BUT Iran AND OMAN manage traffic. WHITE HOUSE: "COMPLETE FABRICATION." TRUMP: "no nation will control shipping" through Hormuz. US-IRAN EXCHANGED FIRE EARLY THURSDAY (CNN 16min ago): US struck Iranian drones + launch site near Hormuz. IRGC fired WARNING SHOTS at FOUR VESSELS near Hormuz (passing "without prior coordination or authorization"). IRAN launched BALLISTIC MISSILES TOWARD KUWAIT — intercepted by CENTCOM. IRGC targeted US AIR BASE at 4:50 AM local time. BRENT: $93.71 Wednesday close (-58 cents) — lowest since mid-March. Rebounding Thursday on fresh fighting. HOCHSTEIN: "No matter what — Iranians will control Hormuz for foreseeable future. Doesn't even matter what the deal says." India Thursday: binary. Trump signs = Brent $85-88, Nifty +800-1,000. Trump rejects = Brent $100+, Nifty -300-400. West Asia War Day 90.

assessment.headline: DAY 120, 8:45AM IST — SHARPEST ESCALATION SINCE THE OPENING: IRAN STRUCK US BASES IN KUWAIT (ALI AL SALEM) AND BAHRAIN (5TH FLEET HQ) EARLY SUN JUN 28, RETALIATING FOR A 2ND US STRIKE WAVE THAT FOLLOWED IRAN'S DRONE HIT ON THE KIKU TANKER. US SAYS ALL OF IRAN'S MISSILES/DRONES WERE INTERCEPTED — NO US INJURIES; BAHRAIN REPORTED A DAMAGED BUILDING, NO DEATHS. TRUMP THREATENED TO 'COMPLETE THE JOB'; IRAN THREATENED TO HALT TALKS — YET DECONFLICTION + MOU TALKS STAY ACTIVE. OIL (~$72 FRI) SET TO SPIKE MON; INDIA MARKETS SHUT, REOPEN JUN 29.
assessment.body:
Sunday 8:45 AM IST. Day 120. The most dangerous weekend since the spring — but the deal is, just barely, still standing.

THE WEEKEND'S EXCHANGE
Saturday: an Iranian drone hit the tanker Kiku (2M+ barrels) on the
US/Oman southern route; the US struck Iranian military sites in reply.
Early Sunday: Iran fired ballistic missiles and drones at US bases —
Ali Al Salem in Kuwait and the Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain.
It is the third US strike round in three weeks, and Iran's sharpest reply.

WHAT ACTUALLY LANDED
Far less than Iran claimed. A US official told CNN every drone and missile
was shot down, intercepted, or failed to reach its target — no US injuries.
Kuwait intercepted two ballistic missiles, no damage.
Bahrain: a drone damaged a residential building near the airport, no deaths,
not near the 5th Fleet HQ. Qatar lost one citizen to shrapnel.
Iran's claim of 'eight US sites destroyed' is unverified and looks inflated.

TWO THREATS, ONE OPEN LINE
Trump warned the US could be 'forced to militarily complete the job' —
'the Islamic Republic of Iran will no longer exist.'
Iran threatened a 'complete halt' to talks and more attacks on ships.
And yet: a US official says MoU talks remain on track, no meetings cancelled,
deconfliction channels active, and CENTCOM says transits continue.
The fight is over Article 5 — who administers Hormuz — not the whole deal.

WHY IT HASN'T BROKEN — YET
Both sides are still choosing calibrated strikes over all-out war,
and both still want the 60-day MoU. The new flashpoint is the US-Navy move
to expand the Omani route, which Iran says only delays the reopening.
The next 72 hours decide whether this stays contained.

FOR INDIA
Markets are shut — weekend, after Friday's Muharram holiday —
so there is no live reaction; the last close (Jun 25) was Sensex 77,100,
Nifty ~24,056. Monday Jun 29 prices it all at once: a likely gap-down,
and oil (Brent ~$72 Friday) set to spike after strikes on Gulf bases.
Kuwait hosts ~1M Indians and Bahrain several hundred thousand; the strikes
hit military bases, not civilians, and no Indian casualties are reported.
Base case: the deconfliction line holds and the MoU survives.
Downside: a mass-casualty strike or a halt to talks re-closes Hormuz.
Watch three things: Iran's next move, the Monday reopen, and Brent vs $80.

timeline.tag: WAR BEGINS. US-Israel strike Iran. Supreme Leader Khamenei killed. Hormuz closed within hours.
Hormuz near-total closure confirmed. Brent spiked to $120 briefly. India emergency measures begin.
Brent $108. First India fuel hike (petrol +Rs6/L, diesel +Rs5/L). PM Modi: use energy with restraint.
CEASEFIRE AGREED — US-Iran 2-week pause. Brent fell 16% to $92. Sensex +3,500 pts gap-up. Hormuz nominally reopening.
CEASEFIRE DAY 1. Strait of Hormuz declared open for safe passage. Both crew rescued. Diplomacy begins.
US NAVAL BLOCKADE imposed on Iran ports. Dual blockade. Ceasefire extended indefinitely by Trump.
Second India fuel hike (petrol +Rs5, diesel +Rs4). Islamabad talks collapse. Iran rejects MOU.
Sensex +232 to 75,415. Nifty +65 to 23,719. Week 12 close. Rubio: tentative progress. Iran uranium stays.
TRUMP: deal largely negotiated. RUBIO: days away. PGSA controlled zone graphic. Brent $100.
Trump edited MOU — new uranium/Hormuz demands 'not received well' in Tehran. Iran denied deal. US Defense Secretary combat-ready.
ESCALATION: US struck Qeshm Island. Iran retaliated — 13 missiles + 17 drones at Kuwait + Bahrain. Kuwait Airport hit: 1 Indian killed. Iran halted mediators. House war powers 215-208.
Nifty 23,355 (-0.22%). Sensex 74,219 (-0.17%). Trump: deal 'over the weekend.' Iran halted mediators. US seeks written nuclear commitments. LPG third hike: Rs941.50.
Iran fired 7 ballistic missiles at Kuwait+Bahrain. CENTCOM intercepted 6. Oman terminal explosion. Hezbollah rejected US ceasefire. RBI held 5.25%, 5-pronged FII plan. US S&P -2.64%.

IRAN FIRED MISSILES AT ISRAEL overnight — all intercepted. Israel struck Mahshahr petrochemical complex (first energy strike since ceasefire). Nifty -1.04% (-244 pts). Sensex -719 pts. BSE -Rs6.31T. Brent $97+ intraday → $94.25 close.

IRAN-ISRAEL PAUSE. Trump: 'Both sides want immediate ceasefire.' Iran willing to stop if Israel stops. Pakistan Naqvi letter to Khamenei. Nifty recovered +0.52%. Brent fell 3.42% to $91.11 on de-escalation signals. Vance: 'very close to deal.'

INDIA'S DARKEST DAY: US Navy struck MT Settebello (Gulf of Oman) — 3 Indian sailors killed (first blockade deaths since Apr 13). MT Jalveer also attacked, 20 safe. MEA summoned US CDA, lodged formal protest. US 2nd night strikes on Iran (Bandar Abbas, Sirik). Iran retaliated Bahrain/Jordan/Kuwait. Trump: Iran 'completely defeated,' will 'pay the price.' Nifty 23,215 (-0.12%). Brent climbing to $95.

BIGGEST RALLY OF THE WAR: Nifty +461 pts (+1.99%) to 23,623. Sensex +1,695 pts (+2.3%) to 75,528. VIX -5.7% to 14.72 (lowest since war began). Brent ~$87, WTI under $85. Pakistan PM: final deal text agreed. Iran FM Araghchi: deal on all fronts including Lebanon. US shot down Iranian drones in Hormuz Fri night.

DEAL IMMINENT DAY 105. Trump Sat: 'Deal signed TOMORROW (Jun 14) + Hormuz OPEN TO ALL immediately.' Pakistan PM: 'electronic signing ready, finalisation next 24 hrs, technical talks next week.' Iran FM: NOT Sunday but 'coming days.' Nuclear terms: Iran says no nuclear issues in MOU; CBS sources say 15-20yr lockout included. US shot down more Iran drones in Hormuz Sat. Trump: 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE.' Israel blocking asset unfreezing, not leaving Lebanon. Khamenei funeral announced July 4. Rubio-Jaishankar: US defended Settebello; India MEA: 'lethal force unacceptable.' G7 from Monday.

DAY 106 SUN 7:15AM IST. DEAL SIGNING EXPECTED TODAY per Trump. Iran FM says NOT today but 'coming days.' Pakistan: 'electronic signing ready.' Nuclear ambiguity: public vs private MOU positions diverge. Israel blocking. G7 from Monday (Modi-Trump bilateral). If deal + Hormuz open: Brent $78-82, Nifty 24,500-25,000. Biggest day of the war's diplomatic timeline.

THE DEAL IS DONE. Trump Sun Jun 14 evening: 'Deal with Iran is now complete. Hormuz OPEN TO ALL. Let the oil flow! Naval blockade lifted immediately.' Pakistan PM: 'Peace Deal REACHED.' Iran SNSC: warfare ends immediately on all fronts including Lebanon. Formal signing: Friday Jun 19 Switzerland. Iran Deputy FM: deal is a 'victory.' Nuclear terms: ambiguous. Israel-Lebanon: won't withdraw. Pre-implementation (mine removal) discussions begin.

TWO-DAY WAR-END RALLY COMPLETE: Nifty +231 pts (+0.98%) to 23,854. Sensex +736 pts (+0.97%) to 76,264. Rupee +40 paise. Brent $83.82 (-5%). WTI near $80. Nikkei +5.42%. Realty +2.75% top India sector. Two-day total: Nifty +692 pts, Sensex +2,432 pts. Trump at G7 with Macron: 'Deal's all signed.' Israel refuses Lebanon withdrawal. Modi-Trump G7 bilateral (Settebello). Mine removal begins.

DAY 108 TUE 7:00AM IST. War effectively over. Pre-implementation discussions: mine removal, shipping corridor clearance. Formal signing: Friday Jun 19 Switzerland. Key risk: Israel-Lebanon clause (Israel refuses to withdraw). India: fuel cut likely in 2-3 weeks, Rupee Rs93-94, FII inflows Rs15,000-25,000 Cr expected. 18,000+ Indian seafarers: repatriation window open. G7 continues (Modi-Trump bilateral on Settebello).

DAY 109 WED 8:00AM IST. BURGENSTOCK SIGNING CONFIRMED: Fri Jun 19, near Lucerne Switzerland. Vance + Qalibaf confirmed signatories. Nifty Tue 23,989 (+0.57%) — BRIEFLY CROSSED 24,000 FIRST TIME SINCE WAR. Sensex 76,808 (+0.71%). THREE-DAY RALLY: +827 pts Nifty, +3,281 pts Sensex. Brent ~$79 Tue (-3.2%), low $79.61 — sub-$80 first time since March. MOU: $12B to Iran, $300B fund disputed. Nuclear talks begin after signing. Israel: Ben-Gvir 'not bound' but Lebanese army deployed + residents returning. 48 hrs to signing.

FOUR-DAY RALLY COMPLETE. Nifty Wed Jun 17: 24,085.70 (+0.40%) — FIRST CLOSE ABOVE 24,000 SINCE WAR BEGAN. Sensex 77,155.62 (+0.45%). VIX 13.18 — lowest of war. Four-day total: Nifty +3.99%, Sensex +4.50%. Brent Tue Jun 16: $78.96 (-5%, first below $80 since March). WTI $76.05. 3 Iranian tankers (~5M bbl) exited US blockade — first Iranian oil exports in 2 months. Fed held rates (Chair Warsh). Dow all-time close 51,999. Oil sanctions waiver confirmed immediate after signing (WSJ). Further US-Iran talks begin Switzerland Jun 19.

DAY 111 — SIGNING DAY. Burgenstock MOU ceremony: Vance + Qalibaf. Oil sanctions waiver IMMEDIATE. Further talks begin in Switzerland. Brent $78.92 (Thu open). Nifty above 24,000. Mine removal begins. 3 Iranian tankers already exiting blockade. Full Hormuz normalisation: 4-8 weeks. India: petrol cut Rs4-6/L + LPG Rs80-100/cyl imminent. Rupee Rs91-93 target. The 111-day war ends formally today.

CORRECTION: MOU actually signed Wed Jun 17 at VERSAILLES — Trump + Iran President Pezeshkian, heads of state, 2 days early. Pakistan PM: blockade lifted + Hormuz reopened, 'immediate effect.' Burgenstock today = 60-day talks kickoff, not signing. 14-point MOU revealed: no nukes reaffirmed, uranium down-blended under IAEA (mechanism TBD), Hormuz 'will not return to pre-war conditions' — fee model persists. $300B fund denied by Trump. Khamenei authorised reluctantly. US lawmakers flag verification + missile programme gaps. Brent $78.31 (-1.6%), WTI $74.75.

DAY 112 SAT — IRAN RE-CLOSES HORMUZ. Khatam al-Anbiya military command declares the strait 'closed to vessel traffic' under 48 hrs after the Islamabad MOU, citing a US 'breach' of Article 1 (Israeli strikes in S. Lebanon, no withdrawal) — calls it the 'first step,' warns of more. US/CENTCOM + VP Vance DISPUTE it: 'the straits really are open.' Iran's own FM said hours earlier shipping was 'operating normally.' Oil kept flowing over the weekend (Bloomberg). Brent ~$80.6.

DAY 113 SUN — Switzerland talks suspended after a single round; Iran demands a verified Lebanon ceasefire as a condition and excludes its nuclear programme from the agenda. Trump renews threats of US strikes 'unless Iran curbs its proxies in Lebanon,' threatens Hormuz tolls, warns Tehran against closing the strait. UKMTO: a tanker approached by a skiff with 5 armed individuals ~50nm SE in the Gulf of Oman. ~515 vessels anchored/stopped. Brent ~$81.5 (+1.4%).

DAY 114 MON 10AM IST — Hormuz remains contested: Iran declares it closed, US says open, oil physically still moving. Crude opened the week ~+1.5% (Brent ~$81.5, WTI ~$78). India: Nifty ~24,108 (+0.39%), Sensex ~77,112 (+0.40%) — broadly steady, treating the closure as posturing for now, but the four-day relief rally has stalled. straits.live crisis-pressure 92 (extreme). The 60-day peace clock is in serious doubt.

DAY 115 TUE 8AM IST — CONTESTED DE-ESCALATION. Hormuz stays Iran-declared-closed, but markets shrug it off: CENTCOM says 55 ships transited Jun 20 (~16-17M barrels, a record) and tankers sailed Monday; CENTCOM: 'Iran does not control the Strait.' Switzerland talks resumed Sunday → 60-day roadmap + US-Iran safe-passage line; Trump: 'NO TOLLS' for 60 days unless the US imposes them. Brent FELL ~3.6-4.3% to ~$78.1. India closed Jun 22 UP (Sensex 77,094 +0.38%, Nifty 24,103 +0.37%); 3 Indian tankers (860,000+ MT) crossed safely. SEPARATE NON-WAR: a technical blast at Qatar's Ras Laffan/Barzan facility killed 13 — all Indian & Pakistani nationals; LNG exports unaffected. Live risks: Iran ratification vote ~Jun 23-25, Netanyahu's refusal to leave S. Lebanon, insurance ~8x pre-crisis.

DAY 115 TUE 9PM IST — PM REVISION: risk-off returns. Indian equities sold off despite cheaper oil — Sensex -893.39 (-1.16%) to 76,200.68, Nifty ~-1.16% to ~23,824 — after Trump threatened to resume strikes and Iran briefly walked away from the Switzerland talks; IT (Accenture overhang) + Reliance led the drop. BUT structure firmed: first Burgenstock round concluded with a Qatar/Pakistan 60-day roadmap + four working groups (Sanctions, Nuclear, Reconstruction, Monitoring); US Treasury issued a 60-day Iranian-oil license (incl. US imports, dollar-payable). Brent eased to ~$77 (WTI ~$74) as Gulf flows accelerated. Hormuz still Iran-declared-closed on paper but tankers moving under the Jun 21 safe-passage line. Still fragile: ratification vote awaited, Lebanon unresolved, insurance ~8x.

DAY 116 WED — DE-ESCALATION ACCELERATES. Hormuz transits surge: Kpler reports ~4.8M bpd flowing (most since Feb 28), ~70 ships transited Wed (+105% day-on-day), 20+ long-stranded tankers (~35M barrels) exit the Gulf; the Joint Maritime Information Center cuts the Hormuz threat to 'moderate' and the US Treasury waives Iranian-oil sanctions through August. India recovers: Sensex +790.54 (+1.04%) to 76,991.22, Nifty +197.55 to 24,021.65. Brent sliding toward ~$75.

DAY 117 THU — OIL HITS A 4-MONTH LOW, THEN A SHIP IS HIT. Brent falls to ~$72 (lowest since late Feb, near the ~$70 pre-war level, >10% down on the week) as Gulf flows accelerate. THEN an Iranian one-way attack drone strikes the Singapore-flagged container ship Ever Lovely as it exits Hormuz on the US/Oman southern corridor near Oman — Trump says Iran fired 4 drones (3 shot down), 1 hit the upper deck, no injuries. The IMO PAUSES its plan to evacuate ~11,000 stranded seafarers. India closes marginally up: Sensex 77,100.47 (+0.14%), Nifty ~24,056.

DAY 118 FRI 9:15AM IST — RE-ESCALATION: US STRIKES IRAN. At Trump's direction, CENTCOM hits four targets — Iranian missile and drone storage + coastal radar along Iran's coast (six aircraft, around Sirik) — in retaliation for the Jun 25 drone attack on the Ever Lovely, calling it 'unwarranted aggression' that violated the ceasefire. The ~2-week pause in US offensive ops ends; the Jun 17 MOU is under immediate strain. Trump warns of more; Iran vows a harsh response. Oil bounces from a ~$72 low toward ~$74. India markets SHUT for Muharram; reopen Mon Jun 29.

DAY 119 SAT — 2nd SHIP ATTACK + 2nd US STRIKE WAVE. An Iranian one-way drone hits the Panama-flagged tanker Kiku (2M+ barrels) at ~4:30am ET on the US/Oman southern route; CENTCOM then strikes Iranian military targets near Hormuz (surveillance, comms, air defence, drone storage, minelayers) at Sirik, Bandar-e Lengeh and Qeshm. Trump: struck 'for violating the Cease Fire Agreement, AGAIN!' and warns the US could 'complete the job' — 'the Islamic Republic of Iran will no longer exist!' Markets closed (weekend); Brent frozen at ~$72.

DAY 120 SUN 8:45AM IST — IRAN STRIKES US BASES IN KUWAIT & BAHRAIN. Early Sun the IRGC fires ballistic missiles and drones at the US Ali Al Salem Air Base (Kuwait) and the US Fifth Fleet HQ at Port Salman (Bahrain), retaliating for the 2nd US strike wave; claims (unverified) 8 US sites destroyed. US: all intercepted, NO US injuries; Kuwait downs 2 ballistic missiles; Bahrain reports a damaged residential building, no deaths; 1 Qatari killed by shrapnel. Trump threatens to 'complete the job'; Iran threatens a 'complete halt' to talks — yet deconfliction + MoU talks stay active and CENTCOM says transits continue. Oil (~$72 Fri) set to gap up Mon; India markets shut (weekend/Muharram), reopen Mon Jun 29.
